summary: An unnamed first-person narrator, injured from earlier violence, leaps across a roughly thirteen-foot gap from one rooftop to a neighboring building, landing in rubble. They then pick their way across the wrecked third floor, descend a ladder-like staircase into a skylight opening, and survey a second floor that had been set up as a gang barracks with bunks and a kitchen stocked with MREs. The passage is a fiction excerpt from Book 6, part 48, emphasizing tension, caution about booby traps, and physical pain.
one_line: A wounded narrator leaps a thirteen-foot gap between rooftops, then cautiously explores a rubble-strewn building that served as a gang's barracks.
key_facts: The vertical distance between the two roofs was barely over thirteen feet.
The narrator tosses bits of roof over the landing area to check whether anything is still live before jumping.
The narrator runs at the roof edge, cannot see the landing spot, and sees only purple-blue sky.
The narrator lands exactly where aimed on the third floor of the other building and rolls out.
The narrator recalls prior injuries: napalm, street-sized bonfires, being shot, and an intentional car crash.
The narrator coughs and their ribs twinge after the landing.
The third floor is described as a broad forest of rubble and nubs of walls, with a broken computer monitor and a dismembered office chair among the debris.
The narrator stays wary of explosives that were not part of the original blast.
The narrator finds a staircase that is more like a ladder into a skylight and descends carefully, worried about rigged walls or floors.
The second floor was set up like a barracks with bunks stacked in many rooms with no privacy.
A rusted-out kitchen on the second floor contains boxed MREs, and the narrator doubts its plumbing works.
